findings.description: Candidate schema in openapi/v1.1.yaml only adds agent_id, omitting vendor_type, location, isolation, and dispatch_mode. In SelectModelResponse, alternatives is defined as an array of Candidate objects, preventing alternative candidates from retaining their configured lane assignment dimensions. This violates the spec scenario 'each alternative SHALL retain its own exact agent_id, vendor type, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, and endpoint kind' and design D6.

findings.description: routing-decision.schema.json requires top-level assignment and provenance fields with additionalProperties=false, conflicting directly with both durable persistence mechanisms. The PostgreSQL routing_decisions table (migration 040) stores assignment and provenance inside JSONB fields (selected/request) without top-level columns per design D7, and contains columns (created_at, exploration, fallback, policy_version, budget_state) rejected by additionalProperties=false. Simultaneously, design D7 specifies that the linked coordinator audit event is merely a sanitized index/link with decision ID, selected agent/model, policy version, and source, rather than a full snapshot containing request, assignment, provenance, alternatives, and excluded.

routing-decision.schema.json defines provenance with only 5 fields, omitting matched_rule_ids, rationale, and catalog_key. In contrast, openapi/v1.1.yaml RoutingProvenance and design D6 require all 8 fields. This results in internal contract drift between the API provenance contract and the event schema.

wp-transports-fallback is declared to run concurrently with wp-policy-service (depends_on: [wp-contract-config]), but its scope includes tests/model_routing/test_api.py and src/coordination_mcp.py, which consume the updated SelectModelRequest/SelectModelResponse models and service logic in src/model_routing/api.py. Because api.py is locked and modified exclusively by wp-policy-service, wp-transports-fallback in an isolated branch cannot compile or pass test_api.py against the unmodified api.py, violating package isolation and parallelizability.

findings.description: Design D7 requires coordinator audit event logging to use an awaited durable audit operation that fails the request if durability cannot be established. However, AuditService.log_operation() in agent-coordinator/src/audit.py defaults to async_logging=True fire-and-forget scheduling without a parameter for callers to demand synchronous durable writes or await the insert. Neither tasks.md nor work-packages.yaml specifies adding an explicit durability parameter or sync insert mechanism to AuditService, causing routing calls to silently default to fire-and-forget logging in violation of the durability contract.
findings.existing_code: The write uses an awaited durable audit operation and fails the request if durability cannot be established; fire-and-forget acceptance is insufficient.

findings.description: Design D3 specifies that 'the first matching rule supplies a dimension and phase/default values fill the remainder'. However, routing.schema.json restricts defaults with additionalProperties=false to only dispatch_mode and phase_dispatch_modes. It provides no default fields or phase default mappings for location or isolation when a rule sets only a subset of dimensions.

RoutingProvenance in openapi/v1.1.yaml defines catalog_key as a required 4-element tuple, but design D8 specifies that local fallback (source=local-static) derives assignments purely from routing.yaml, agents.yaml, and static maps without querying the catalog. Neither the contract nor the spec defines how local fallback satisfies this required 4-element catalog key or whether it should be nullable when running in degraded local mode.

Design D5 specifies a deterministic multi-lane tie-breaking sort order of (-score, agent_id, catalog identity), but spec.md omits this tie-breaking behavior and resolver.py currently sorts only by score. Without formal tie-breaking in the spec, candidate ordering is non-deterministic when multiple lanes project identical catalog models with equal utility scores.
